claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-known scientific myth
Neuroimaging techniques such as fMRI and PET scans demonstrate that virtually all parts of the brain are active and utilized throughout daily functioning, even during sleep
Neurological evidence also shows that damage to even tiny, specific areas of the brain can result in severe physical or cognitive impairments, which would not occur if 90% were dormant
Evolutionarily, the brain consumes roughly 20% of the body's energy despite accounting for only 2% of body mass, making the maintenance of a 90% dormant organ biologically untenable.

claim_traces.claim_text: "Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short — around 5 feet 2 inches tall."
reasoning_steps: The belief that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short (around 5 feet 2 inches) is a historical misconception stemming from a confusion between French and British units of measurement, reinforced by contemporary British propaganda (such as caricatures by James Gillray)
At the time of his autopsy, Napoleon was measured at 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French measurements (pieds and pouces)
When converted to modern/English imperial units, his actual height was approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (around 169 cm)
This made him average or slightly above average in height for a French man of the early 19th century.
